title: SSO/RBAC obligations as configurable contract commitments + pricing experiment
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: A growing subset of mid-market and enterprise prospects require contractual commitments around SSO (SAML/OIDC) and role-based access control (RBAC) before procurement. Current offerings are a mix of 'included' features on Enterprise and ad-hoc add-ons negotiated per deal. We need a repeatable, testable packaging approach that balances sales flexibility, legal risk, and engineering cost-of-delivery.

Objective: Run an experiment to evaluate three packaging options for SSO and RBAC commitments and measure impact on win rate, ACV, time-to-close, and support/engineering effort. Produce recommended contract clauses (minimal and preferred), pricing deltas, and an implementation rollout plan if we standardize a package.

Scope: Enterprise customers (>$250k ARR or equivalent procurement size). Technical scope includes SAML 2.0/ OIDC support surface, user-provisioning/SYNC expectations, RBAC primitives (roles, custom roles, role assignment APIs), audit logging availability, and delegated admin controls in Console. Legal scope includes indemnities, uptime commitments for auth flows, and data handling for identity attributes. This ticket covers product and contract design + go/no-go recommendation; implementation work is tracked in ENG follow-ups.

Success metrics (experiment):
- Primary: Relative change in win rate for RFPs where SSO/RBAC is a stated requirement (baseline 2025 H2 win rate).
- Secondary: Median time-to-close, average ACV uplift for deals accepting standardized package vs bespoke add-on, number of legal redlines per contract, engineering effort hours for onboarding.

Constraints and risks:
- Engineering capacity to build hardened SAML connectors and RBAC admin UX within quarter.
- Legal risk of committing SLA on authentication availability without hardened passive failover.
- Sales resistance to a fixed add-on price if competitors bundle SSO for free.

Experiment arms (to be A/B tested across matched opportunities):
1) Inclusive Enterprise: SSO (SAML/OIDC) + basic RBAC included at no additional fee for Enterprise SKUs; contract clause: "SSO and Role Management included as part of Enterprise subscription; Customer responsibilities limited to IdP configuration and identifying role mappings."
2) Add-on SKU: SSO + advanced RBAC packaged as a priced add-on (flat monthly fee + per-seat premium); contract clause: "SSO and RBAC delivered as Add-on; subject to standard support response times; 30-day onboarding window quoted separately."
3) Hybrid: Basic SSO included; advanced RBAC, audit logs, and SCIM user sync offered as paid components. Contract clause: "Basic authentication included; advanced features listed as optional add-ons with separate SLAs and onboarding timelines."

Data to collect: opportunity stage, buyer persona, requirement list, pricing offered, legal redlines, negotiation notes, and time between LOI and signature.

Deliverables:
- Draft contract language for minimal and preferred clauses (legal-reviewed).
- Pricing matrix with suggested list and discounting guidance for channel vs direct.
- Sales enablement playbook + objection handling.
- Rollout plan for engineering/console changes with gating criteria.

Timeline: 5 weeks for experiment design + pilot; 6-10 week measurement window thereafter.

Links to artifacts: see attachments for PRD, draft clauses, and sample pogo spreadsheets.
